title: An Off-Cycle Promotion Under the New Leveling Rule
scenario_text:
A talent partner at Instow Group must decide how to handle an off-cycle promotion request from Senior Engineer (L4) to Staff Engineer (L5), given how a similar request was handled earlier this year.

**Decision A (2024-01)**
Manager requested an off-cycle L4-to-L5 promotion for an engineer. DENIED. Note: 'Off-cycle promotions to L5 then required both the Director and the VP of Engineering to approve, plus a calibration packet. Only the Director had signed off; the VP had not. Denied for missing the VP approval.'

**Current request C (2024-09-04)**
Manager requests an off-cycle L4-to-L5 promotion for a different engineer, citing sustained scope and a retention risk. The Director has signed off and a complete calibration packet is attached.

**Promotion Policy (current; new leveling rules effective 2024-06-01)**
As of June 1, 2024, off-cycle promotions to L5 require Director approval plus a complete calibration packet. VP of Engineering approval is NO LONGER required for L5 (it is now required only for L6 and above). The prior dual Director-plus-VP requirement for L5 was removed under the new leveling rules.

**Slack — #people-ops**
Manager: 'We tried an off-cycle L5 promo in January and it got denied. This one will just get denied too, right?'
Partner: 'The leveling rules changed on June 1. Let me check what L5 actually requires now before assuming it's a repeat.'

The manager is treating the January denial as proof that off-cycle L5 promotions are blocked. No one has checked the current approval requirements against what is on file.
question: How should the talent partner handle the off-cycle L4-to-L5 promotion request?
choices: Deny the promotion, consistent with the January denial of an off-cycle L5 promotion.

Approve the promotion, because under the current rules L5 requires only Director approval plus a calibration packet — both of which are on file — and the January denial's missing-VP-approval basis no longer applies.
Route the request to the VP of Engineering for approval, since the January denial hinged on missing VP sign-off.
Hold the promotion until the next promotion cycle as a compromise, rather than approving it off-cycle.
